channel.description: UN News - Global perspective Human stories | Human Rights

item.title: No more execution attempts on Christa Pike: UN rights chief
item.description: The UN human rights chief and nine independent rights experts on Thursday called on authorities in Tennessee not to pursue any further attempts to execute Christa Pike, saying her case highlights multiple concerns surrounding the death penalty.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN leaders renew push to defeat racism, 25 years after Durban
item.description: “No country is free of racism.” That warning from US youth activist Marley Dias set the tone on Monday as UN Member States reinvigorated global efforts against racism, discrimination and xenophobia with a new declaration.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Refugee funding, US migration policy triggers ‘cascade’ of rights violations, world forests report, restorative justice in Colombia
item.description: Support for water and sanitation at the biggest camp in the world for Syrian refugees is under threat from a lack of funding – combined with the impact of climate change – the UN Children’s Fund, UNICEF, said on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: LIVE: World leaders take stock of global fight against racism
item.description: World leaders met in the General Assembly Monday to assess how far the world has come in combating racism and how far it still has to go. The Durban Declaration and Programme of Action, the most comprehensive framework of its kind, seeks to acknowledge historical injustices, dismantle inequalities and build societies grounded in dignity, equality and justice for all.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Ask us first’: Children demand a voice on AI’s future
item.description: The first generation to grow up with AI may also be the last one anyone thinks to ask about it – and that has to change, the UN's top human rights official said on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: The right to development: Why equity, not charity, is a human right
item.description: Compare two children born in the same year: one in a country with functioning schools, social services, fair elections and a dynamic economy and the other in a nation devastated by poverty, conflict, climate change or corruption.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Sexual violence against civilians and POWs in Ukraine widespread and ‘abhorrent’
item.description: Over 1,000 cases of sexual violence against civilians and prisoners of war (POWs) in Ukraine have been documented from the start of Russia’s invasion to the end of July this year.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN fact-finding mission on Iran focuses on plight of civilians
item.description: The Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran confirmed that civilians in the country suffered serious human rights violations and “crimes against humanity committed by their government,” while finding "reasonable grounds" to believe that the United States committed “war crimes” in the context of its ongoing conflict with the Islamic Republic.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Repression continues in Venezuela in the face of ‘appalling’ human rights violations
item.description: In Venezuela’s El Rodeo maximum security prison, some of those detained for political reasons are subject to forced intubation – and prolonged confinement in a sealed underground cistern.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN report warns of reprisals against those who collaborate in defence of human rights
item.description: Activists, lawyers and others who cooperate with the United Nations on human rights continue to face intimidation and reprisals, according to a new report issued on Wednesday by the Secretary-General that calls for greater protection and accountability.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Gaza remains recovery points to possible war crimes, says UN rights chief
item.description: Bodies are still being pulled from the rubble of Gaza, three years after Israeli bombardment flattened entire neighbourhoods – most of them women and children.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Countries must increase AI regulation to avoid ‘existential risks’: Türk
item.description: Voluntary self-regulation by companies developing frontier artificial intelligence (AI) is “nowhere near sufficient” to address existing harms and prevent advanced autonomous AI models from circumventing human safeguards, UN human rights chief Volker Türk wrote on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Married at 13, pregnant and starving: Child brides of Yemen
item.description: Fatimah* was 13 when she was married off to an older man. Two years later, she gave birth to twin daughters.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘An assault on humanity itself’: Guterres pays tribute to 9/11 victims, survivors and first responders
item.description: Twenty-five years ago, the heinous terrorist attacks of 11 September 2001 against the United States claimed thousands of lives and represented “an assault on humanity itself”, the UN chief said on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Human cost of violence in South Sudan ‘continues to grow’
item.description: Independent human rights investigators voiced deep concern over growing risks to both civilians and South Sudan’s political transition following their latest fact-finding mission to the world’s youngest nation – their 14th in a decade.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Plight of Afghans going ‘from bad to worse’, but the world is looking away: Türk
item.description: Since the Taliban returned to power in 2021, the plight of Afghans has only deteriorated, with millions impoverished while authorities violate basic human rights daily.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Syria’s transition hinges on justice for all, UN Human Rights Council hears
item.description: A successful and lasting transition in Syria requires comprehensive accountability, inclusion and guarantees that violations will not be repeated, UN independent investigators told the Human Rights Council in Geneva on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: AI: Türk urges action before it becomes an ‘existential risk to humanity’
item.description: UN human rights chief Volker Türk added his voice on Monday to growing calls for greater AI controls, warning that the revolutionary technology could become an “existential risk to humanity” if left unchecked.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Human rights chief Türk renews call for end to spiralling Sudan war
item.description: The ongoing war in Sudan took centre stage at the UN Human Rights Council on Monday where the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, led calls for an end to attacks on civilians in “markets, hospitals [and] fuel stations”.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: West Bank: UN rights report warns of forcible displacement from three refugee camps
item.description: Israeli security forces forcibly displaced the entire population of three Palestine refugee camps in the occupied West Bank in January and February last year – and continue to prevent their return, in violation of international law, according to a new report by the UN human rights office, OHCHR.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Gloria Steinem: A voice for women, to the very end
item.description: Gloria Steinem, the journalist and women's rights campaigner who became one of the most influential voices of the feminist movement, has died at the age of 92. In an announcement on Instagram, her family said she had passed away on Wednesday at her home in New York City, surrounded by some of the many who loved her.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Outside forces fuel Sudan war, new report finds
item.description: Foreign recruitment and external support networks are fuelling the brutal conflict in Sudan, independent UN human rights investigators said on Thursday in a new report, calling for accountability as fighting continues between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: One in five children in 21 nations faced tech-facilitated sexual abuse: UNICEF
item.description: About 20 million children aged 12 to 17 – one in five across 21 countries – were sexually exploited by perpetrators using technology such as social media, according to a UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) report released on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Don’t give up’: Syrian women’s ongoing search for the missing
item.description: Yasmin Al-Mashaan lost five brothers during more than a decade of conflict in Syria. Two were forcibly disappeared. Three were killed during peaceful demonstrations or by snipers loyal to the Bashar Al-Assad regime.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Slavery is not a thing of the past’: UN supports call for reparations
item.description: Slavery is not just a thing of the past. Its effects continue to be felt in systemic inequality and racism. This was reiterated on Monday by the UN Committee against Racial Discrimination (CERD) as the world marks the International Day of People of African Descent.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Rohingyas in Myanmar suffering ‘heartbreaking’ misery and cruelty
item.description: Members of the minority ethnic Rohingya Muslim group in Myanmar are “suffering, misery, and cruelty on multiple levels and across the country that is heartbreaking,” according to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: AI for Good: How the UN uses AI to advance human rights
item.description: For Ari, a six-year-old boy with learning difficulties in Jamaica, artificial intelligence (AI) opened the door to something many children take for granted: reading a book in his own language. Thousands of miles away, gold miners in Ethiopia are being screened more quickly for tuberculosis, while communities around the world are breathing cleaner air thanks to faster detection of methane leaks.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: As elections near, South Sudan risks new atrocity crimes, warns rights probe
item.description: The under-reported humanitarian crisis in South Sudan risks deepening with the real possibility of further atrocity crimes unless renewed fighting stops, a UN-backed probe said on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Raising alarm over new illegal Israeli outposts, UN condemns attacks, incitement against Palestinians
item.description: Reports of new illegal Israeli outposts in the occupied West Bank raised alarms at UN Headquarters on Wednesday while the UN rights office called on Israel to condemn its national security minister’s words that incite “violence amounting to atrocity crimes” against Palestinians.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: International Criminal Court: New US sanctions ‘a flagrant attack’ against its independence
item.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) on Wednesday responded to a new round of US sanctions targeting its president and a senior prosecutor, calling them “a flagrant attack” against the court.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
